title: Predictors for Global Perceived Effect in Individuals With Chronic Low Back Pain: A Prospective Observational Study
titleZh: 慢性下背痛患者总体感知疗效的预测因素：一项前瞻性观察研究
abstract: Assessing patient-perceived progression in treatment helps clinicians understand both physical and psychological changes. However, evidence on predictors of the global perceived effect (GPE) scale remains limited. This prospective observational study investigated baseline values and change scores of self-reported outcomes as predictors of GPE in individuals with chronic low back pain (CLBP). A total of 168 CLBP participants completed assessments both at baseline and after 4 weeks, including patient characteristics, disability, self-efficacy, pain catastrophizing, and quality of life. Logistic regression analyses examined associations between these variables and GPE. In multivariable analyses, higher baseline physical function and lower fatigue were significantly associated with improved GPE. Among change scores, only a reduction in disability was significantly related to perceived improvement. These findings suggest that baseline physical function and fatigue, along with disability reduction, have important prognostic relevance for selected patient-reported measures in assessing short-term outcomes in CLBP and may inform clinical decision-making in CLBP management.
